title: Compatible finite quotient bases under inverse image along a pro-etale object
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a scheme $X$, an object $W\to X$ of its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and a module sheaf $L$ over the completed integral coefficient sheaf $R_X$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Suppose $L|_W\cong R_X|_W$ on the slice site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Put $P=L[0]$ and $O=R_{W}[0]$, where $R_W$ is the completed coefficient sheaf on $W.left$. For every $n\ge0$, let $F_n=\operatorname{Res}_n W^*(P\otimes_{R_X}A_{n,X})$ be the actual strict finite pullback complex [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined], and let $G_n$ be the strict identity-coefficient scalar-extension quotient of $O$ [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined]. Here $A_{n,T}$ denotes the constant quotient at exponent $n+1$, restriction is along the completed projection, and both towers retain their prescribed quotient transitions. There exist chain isomorphisms $b_n:F_n\cong G_n$ such that $t^F_n b_n=b_{n+1}t^G_n$ for every $n$, in left-to-right composition order. No local freeness, invertibility of $\ell$ on $X$, boundedness beyond the displayed single complexes, or finiteness of $X$ is assumed.

Proof (3), compatible integral bases reduced to finite coefficient levels

proof.text: For each exponent choose the normalized finite basis c_n supplied by lem-pur-integral-object-finite-basis. Its inverse on a section z is z times the explicitly constructed inverse-image tensor generator of the one integral basis. These inverse formulas uniquely determine c_n.

Identify the prescribed pullback transition with its explicit finite-linear mate. Its unit formula carries the generator at exponent n+2 to the generator at exponent n+1: naturality of the underlying additive presheaf map commutes with restriction along U -> W times_X V, and the original tensor transition sends 1 tensor x to 1 tensor x. Finite semilinearity consequently sends z beta_(n+1) to reduction(z) beta_n. The normalized inverse formulas prove the pullback-basis transition equation.

Use the already proved finite regular scalar multiplication isomorphisms s_n and their transition formula. Restrict c_n and s_n along the completed coefficient projection and put b_n=c_n followed by inverse(s_n). Cancel these isomorphisms to compare the successor square on the regular finite single complex. Outside degree zero its source is zero. In degree zero, the preceding inverse-basis calculation and the scalar multiplication transition formula both give the finite quotient reduction of z. This proves the required chain-map equation.

theorem integralObjectPullbackQuotientBasis (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (W : X.ProEt) (L : integralTowerModules.{u, u} l E X)
    (e : L.over W ≅
      (SheafOfModules.unit.{u, u + 1, u + 1}
        (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted.{u, u} l E X)).over W) :
    ∃ b : ∀ n : ℕ,
      (integralOperationsPullbackLevel.{u, u} l E W.hom n).obj
          ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (integralTowerModules.{u, u} l E X) 0).obj L) ≅
        (integralScalarLevel.{u, u} l E E (AlgHom.id _ _) W.left n).obj
          ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor
              (integralTowerModules.{u, u} l E W.left) 0).obj
            (SheafOfModules.unit.{u, u + 1, u + 1}
              (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted.{u, u} l E W.left))),
      ∀ n : ℕ,
        (integralOperationsPullbackTransition.{u, u} l E W.hom n).app
            ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor
              (integralTowerModules.{u, u} l E X) 0).obj L) ≫ (b n).hom =
          (b (n + 1)).hom ≫
            (integralScalarTransition.{u, u} l E E (AlgHom.id _ _) W.left n).app
              ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor
                  (integralTowerModules.{u, u} l E W.left) 0).obj
                (SheafOfModules.unit.{u, u + 1, u + 1}
                  (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted.{u, u} l E W.left)))
